paragraphs.source_en: Do you ever feel as if no one wants to make a decision, or that you are always talking to the wrong person in a company? Even though selling to buying groups, boards, or committees is a common scenario today, you must remember that companies do not make decisions—people do. Yet, because of competing interests within an organization, it is often difficult to determine who really has the final say on a purchase and who has the greatest influence during the decision-making process. When you are offered a response such as, ‘‘I need to talk it over with Mike,’’ you remember all of these factors and ask the questions that will help you clear up some of the confusion.
